texts.preamble: Anil Kumar vs Megha Engineering And Infrastructure on 28 April, 2025 Kabc020034882024 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 28th Day Of April 2025
texts.facts: 02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: On 15.11.2023 at about 07.00 a.m, the petitioner was driving his Goods vehicle bearing No. KA-16-D-5474 on the left side of Challakere to Parashurampura Road, when he reached near Kaimara (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.601/2024 Gate, Air out, at that time the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-7845 drove his lorry in high speed, rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against the right side of the petitioner's vehicle. Due to this the right hand of the petitioner was detached from his body and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Challakere Government hospital, wherein after necessary treatment and examinations the wounds are found and further he was shiftede to St. John's hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient from 15.11.2023 to 07.12.2023 and underwent surgery in the form of debridement and revision amputation of right upper limb, open reduction and internal fixation of IMIL Nail for femur fracture and other injuries were treated with necessary medications and discharged with an advice to take follow-up treatment regularly and has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and he has to undergo one more surgery in future, for which he has to incur further medical expenses and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and was Driver by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.601/2024 accidental injuries, now he is bedridden and under treatment, due to which he is not able to do any work and suffering from permanent disability and also lost his marriage prospectus, which resulted in loss of income. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper Lorry involved in the accident and in this regard the Challakere Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending Tipper Lorry. Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Tipper Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs. 03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence, was placed exparte. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement. Anil Kumar vs Megha Engineering And Infrastructure on 28 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175305460/ 2 04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and contended that the offending vehicle had no permit at the time of accident and the alleged offending vehicle was used on public road without valid permit and there is a violation of policy terms and conditions (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.601/2024 and provisions of M.V. Act and admits that this respondent has issued a policy bearing No.431301/31/2024/1005 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing No. KA-07-A-7845 and their liability if any, is strictly in terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and further contended that the driver of lorry did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident and the owner has knowingly allowed the person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1 and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner. The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant. Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs. 06. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 and through them got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 and closed the petitioner side evidence. The respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer and Superintendent, RTO as RW.1 and 2 and through them got marked 9 documents as Ex.R.1 to 9 and closed its side evidence. REASONS 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein. Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner. 10. Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained right arm traumatic amputation and fracture shaft femur right and he assessed permanent physical (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.601/2024 disability for right lower limb at 51% and permanent physical disability for right upper limb at 95% and further he stated that petitioner needs surgery for implant removal right femur and right trans humeral myoelectric prosthesis, which may cost approximately Rs.5,00,000/- and he has produced Disability assessment proforma, X-rays and X-ray report as per Ex.P.17 to 19. During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that before the petitioner came to his hospital, he is already undergone surgery for amputation right arm and admits that in the wound certificate femur fracture is not mentioned and he was taken complete treatment at St.John's hospital. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.45,69,463/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
texts.arguments: The respondent No.2 has relied upon the citation reported in No.3297/2019 (MV-D) in a case of Nadilakshmamma and others V/s Raju.B and another, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that in a case of if driver had no driving licence, under such circumstances, it is held that Insurance Company cannot fastened liability of pay and recover when there is clearly breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself. The said citation is pertaining to non-possession of driving licence and not pertaining to permit. 31. The respondent No.2 also relied upon another citation reported in MFA No.1662/2023 (MV-D) in a case of Chandrakala and another V/s Dilipkumar.M.A and another, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the Insurance Company to pay interest on loss of future prospects. Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects. Anil Kumar vs Megha Engineering And Infrastructure on 28 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175305460/ 8 32. The respondent No.2 also relied upon another citation reported in MFA No.30759/2009 (SCCH-3) 20 M.V.C.No.601/2024 (WC) c/w MFA No.32039/2010 (WC) in a case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Susheelabai and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka also held that driver not holding valid driving licence to drive the vehicle, it is clear breach of policy conditions by the owner of the vehicle, hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation. But said Judgment is not pertaining with respect of permit. 33. The respondent No.2 also relied upon another citation reported in AIR 2004 SC 4882 in a case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Challa Upendra Rao and others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that plying of vehicle without valid permit - it amounts to infraction of law - Accident caused - Said defence would be available to insurer - Person without permit to ply vehicle cannot be placed at better pedestal vis-a-vis one who had permit, but has violated condition thereof - insurer consequently would not be liable to pay compensation. (B) Accident compensation - Insurer proved to be not liable to pay compensation - It (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.601/2024 may initiate proceeding before executing Couirt as if dispute between insurer and owner was subject matter of determination before tribunal and issue is decided against owner/insurer. In the said citation the Hon'ble Supreme Court itself held that in case plying of vehicle without valid permit, then it would be proper for insurer to satisfy the award though it had no liability. 34. The respondent No.2 also relied upon another citation reported in 2016 (2) AKR 351 in a case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s S.N.Somashekar and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that driver plying the vehicle beyond area of transport limit at relevant time - Liability cannot be saddled on Insurance Company. But as per the citation relied upon by the respondent No.2 itself in a case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Challa Upendra Rao and others, clearly held that considering beneficial object of Act, it would be proper for insurer to satisfy award, though in law it had no liability and pay and recovery order can be passed. 35. Further, in a Civil Appeal No.2253/2018 (SC) Amrit Paul Singh and another V/s Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, Therefore, the (SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.601/2024 tribunal as well as the High Court had directed the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver. The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh (supra) and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle. (para 23) - wherein offending vehicle had no permit, in such a case the Hon'ble Apex Court directed the insurer to satisfy the Award and insurer has given the option and liberty to recover the same from owner and driver. 36. In MFA 202022/2016 dt:08.07.2022 in a case of Dr.Narasimulu Nandini Memorial Education Trust, Raichur V/s The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka (Kalaburagi Bench) wherein the vehicle had no FC and Permit, it is held that An insurer cannot Anil Kumar vs Megha Engineering And Infrastructure on 28 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175305460/ 9 escape from the liability of paying compensation even when the fitness certificate and Permit of a vehicle is not renewed, but the insurance policy is in force. The High Court has directed the Insurance Company to indemnify the school bus owner by paying the entire compensation amount. 37. In MFA 7391/2013 dt:28.06.2021 in a case of The Secretary, Bapuji Vidya Samsthe , Shivamogga V/s Umeshanaika and others, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that insurer is liable even if the vehicle lacks FC, not having a valid FC was not a fundamental breach. The main contention of this Insurance Company that inspite of no Permit to ply the vehicle in that place and no FC, the tribunal committed an error in fastening the liability. In the said decision it is further held in para 9 that, "In view of the Judgments of this Court in MFA No.6021/2006 (MV) dt:08.03.2010, MFA No.6311/2014 (MV) dt:02.12.2014 and MFA No.8573/2014 (MV) dt:02.09.2015, held that, even in the absence of Fitness Certificate, the Insurance Company cannot contend that they are not liable to pay the compensation when there was a contract of Insurance and the other policy conditions are fulfilled.
